dimension: South Bay / Bay Area ski & snowboard rental shops — what a 4-ski-day package (skis or board + boots + poles) actually costs out the door for a San Jose group driving to Tahoe, and whether the site's unverified $20/day estimate survives contact with published 2026-27 rate cards

findings.name: Sports Basement (Sunnyvale + Campbell) — Adult Basic Ski/Board Package — THE HEADLINE NUMBER
findings.claim: Sports Basement's live Snow Rental Rates table, fetched 2026-08-27, prices the Adult Basic Ski/Board Package on a four-column duration grid whose headers read verbatim: 'day (1 day)', 'weekend (2-4 days)', 'week (5-9 days)', 'season (through June 5th)'. Adult Basic = $50 / $85 / $145 / $290. A 4-ski-day trip lands squarely in the 'weekend (2-4 days)' bracket at $85 flat — $21.25 per ski day. This is the single most decision-relevant number in this dimension, because Sports Basement is the only chain with TWO stores physically in the South Bay: Sunnyvale (1177 Kern Ave, Sunnyvale CA 94085, (408) 598-4240) and Campbell (1875 S Bascom Ave Suite 240, The Pruneyard, Campbell CA 95008, (408) 899-5783). Both store pages explicitly advertise snow rentals — the Campbell page says 'Visit our Campbell store or reserve your snow rentals online today! All rentals can be found in our rentals department in the back left corner of the store'. Crucially, the duration brackets are NOT per-day charges: going from 1 day ($50) to 4 days ($85) costs only $35 more for three extra days, so the marginal cost of ski days 2-4 is about $11.67/day. Sports Basement's own snow-season guide states the transport-day rule in its own words: 'when you rent from Sports Basement, your pickup and return days are free! F-R-E-E. We know it's tough to travel to and from the mountains, and we just don't think you ought to pay extra for those transport days.' That means a Thursday-evening pickup and a Tuesday return around four ski days still bills as a 4-day rental. NOTE ON PRICE MOVEMENT: cached/secondary copies of this same page still circulating in search results show the older Adult Basic figures of $45 day / $70 weekend / $155 week / $260 season and a variant $45 / $80 / $135 / $270. The live page today shows $50 / $85 / $145 / $290 — the rate card has been revised upward, so any figure sourced from a search snippet rather than the live page is stale. The page itself carries NO season-year label (the season column just says 'through June 5th' with no year), but the Sports Basement homepage is actively running 'PREORDER YOUR 2026/27 SNOW GEAR!', so the site is in 26/27 mode and this is the currently posted rate.
findings.price_usd: $85 for the 2-4 day bracket (Adult Basic Ski/Board Package); $50 for 1 day; $145 for 5-9 days; $290 season
findings.restrictions: Duration bracket is 2-4 days, so a 5th ski day jumps the whole rental to the 'week' price of $145 — the 5th day costs $60 by itself. Pickup and return (travel) days are free per Sports Basement's own statement. 'Online reservations have a minimum lead time to ensure your gear will be available at the store you choose. Many same-day rentals are available in store, but the selection may be limited.' No deposit or damage-waiver amount is published on the rates page. Basementeer membership advertises '10% off every purchase' but the site does not state whether that applies to rentals — do not assume it does.
findings.season_confirmed: Live posted rate as of 2026-08-27. The rate table itself carries no season-year label; the site is in 2026-27 mode (homepage promotes '2026/27 snow gear' preorders). Treat as the current posted 26/27 rate, not an explicitly labeled one.
findings.drive_time_from_san_jose: Sunnyvale store ~11 mi / ~18 min from downtown San Jose; Campbell store ~7 mi / ~13 min. Both are in-town pickups requiring no detour on trip day.

The Adult Basic Ski/Board Package row is $50 / $85 / $145 / $290. All four figures are correct, as are the bracket definitions. The $21.25/ski-day and $11.67 marginal-day arithmetic both check out.

The site is simultaneously selling 2026/27 preorders and still publishing last season's guide. The free-days policy is a standing operational convention rather than a 26/27-labelled promise; very likely to hold, but not restated on the 26/27 rate card.

findings.name: VERDICT ON BILL'S $20/DAY ESTIMATE — it survives, but only as a floor, and only for basic gear
findings.claim: The site's unverified $20/day placeholder is defensible but sits exactly at the cheapest edge of the real range, and it mis-models the cost shape. Across every South Bay shop with a published multi-day rate card, a 4-ski-day BASIC adult package prices out at $80-$94 total, i.e. $20.00-$23.50 per ski day: Ski Renter of Mountain View $80 ($20.00/day), Sports Basement $85 ($21.25/day), Outback Adventures Fremont $94 ($23.50/day, on a 25/26 sheet). California Ski Company in Berkeley is cheaper still at $70 ($17.50/day) but is out of the South Bay. So $20/day is the FLOOR, not the median — $21-24/day is the honest South Bay number, and rounding to $20 understates a 6-person group by roughly $30-$85 for the trip. More importantly, $20/day is the wrong SHAPE: no South Bay shop charges per day. They all charge a flat bracket price for the whole rental period, and every one of them gives pickup and return days free. The marginal cost of ski days 2, 3 and 4 at Sports Basement is about $11.67/day, not $20. A per-day model will therefore overprice short trips and underprice the tier upgrade. The bigger risk to the $20 number is TIER, not shop: $20-21/day buys entry-level 'Basic' gear. The Sport/Premium tier a competent skier would actually want is $110 for 4 days at Sports Basement ($27.50/day) and $115 at Outback ($28.75/day) — roughly 30-40% more. If the site's $20/day is meant to cover a mixed group of six, some of whom will upgrade, the blended realistic figure is closer to $22-25/day.
findings.price_usd: $80-$85 total for 4 ski days, basic adult package, South Bay shops with currently-posted rates (Ski Renter $80, Sports Basement $85); Outback's $94 is a 2025-26 price and is excluded from the current range
findings.per_day_usd: $20.00-$21.25 basic from currently-posted South Bay rate cards; $27.50 sport (Sports Basement). Outback's $23.50 basic / $28.75 performance are 2025-26 figures.
findings.restrictions: All figures are adult basic-tier packages of skis-or-board + boots + poles. Helmets are extra almost everywhere ($15/day or $20 for 2-4 days at Sports Basement; $21 for 4-5 days at Outback). Snow apparel is extra again. None of these totals include a helmet, so an out-the-door number for a first-timer is roughly $20-30 higher per person.
findings.season_confirmed: Synthesis of rates posted as of 2026-08-27; component sources vary in season labeling — see individual findings. Outback's contribution is an explicitly 2025-26 sheet.

verification.why: The reasoning and every per-shop component check out against live pages, and the arithmetic is right. But the headline RANGE is built on a season mismatch: its upper bound of $94 is Outback Adventures' 2025-26 price, taken from a rate sheet still explicitly headed '2025-2026 Season'. Mixing a stale-season figure into a range presented as current is exactly the failure mode this project guards against.
verification.correction: Restricted to shops with a CURRENTLY POSTED rate card, the range is $80-$85 for 4 ski days ($20.00-$21.25/ski day): Ski Renter of Mountain View $80 and Sports Basement $85. Outback's $94 is a 2025-26 number and must be captioned as such wherever it appears. California Ski Company's $70 ($17.50/day) remains the cheapest verified 4-day rate but is Berkeley, not South Bay.
verification.net_effect: The conclusion survives and actually tightens: $20/day is the FLOOR, and the honest currently-postable South Bay figure is $20.00-$21.25/day for basic gear, not $20.00-$23.50. The structural criticism - that no South Bay shop charges per day and a per-day model is the wrong shape - is fully confirmed.
verification.confidence_downgraded: high -> medium, because the stated range blends a 2025-26 price with 2026-27-era ones.

findings.name: The Ski Renter of Mountain View — cheapest genuine South Bay shop, and an exact $20/day match
findings.claim: A family-owned, appointment-based rental specialist at 897 Independence Avenue 1C, Mountain View, CA 94043, (650) 961-1414 — the closest dedicated (non-big-box) ski rental shop to San Jose. Its adult price page lists a 1-day Basic package at $45 including 'Skis, Boots, and Poles', then a 2-4 day Basic rate of $80 for 'skis, boots, and poles', a 'Week' (5-9 days) rate of $135, and a Season Lease at $275. At the 2-4 day bracket a 4-ski-day trip works out to exactly $20.00/day — an exact match for the site's placeholder, which is probably where that number came from. The shop states its day-counting rule verbatim: 'We do not count the Pickup day or Return day by 2pm as rental days', with the caveat 'Returns after 2pm will be charged an additional day'. Tier ladder from the main site: Junior Package $35/day, Adult Basic $45/day, Adult Sport $70/day, Adult Performance $90/day ('Skis, Boots (90 Flex or higher), and Poles'). Multi-day rates are published only for the Basic tier — the Sport and Performance tiers show a 1-day price only, so a 4-day sport package cannot be priced from the site. The site notes it is 'By Appointment Only' and that 'Reservations may be made on this website as well as appointments for fitting of your equipment.'
findings.price_usd: $80 for 2-4 days (Adult Basic); $45 1 day; $135 for 5-9 days; $275 season lease
findings.restrictions: By appointment only — this is not a walk-in-on-your-way-out-of-town shop, which matters for a 6-person group needing six boot fittings. Return must be by 2pm or you are charged an extra day, a materially worse rule than Outback's return-by-closing. Multi-day pricing published for Basic tier only; Sport ($70) and Performance ($90) are quoted per-day with no multi-day bracket shown. No deposit amount published. No snowboard-specific price page was reachable (the snowboard price URL 404s), so board pricing is unconfirmed.
findings.season_confirmed: Not stated. The page carries no season-year label and no season date range beyond the 'Season Lease' product. Rates were live as of 2026-08-27.
findings.drive_time_from_san_jose: ~14 mi / ~20 min from downtown San Jose via US-101 or CA-85. In-town pickup, but appointment-only so it must be scheduled ahead.

verification.why: The live adult price page shows Basic Adult Package $45 (1 day) / $80 (2-4 day) / $135 (week 5-9 days) / $275 (season lease) - all four exactly as claimed. The day-counting rule is verbatim: 'We do not count the Pickup day or Return day by 2pm as rental days', and the page separately states 'After 2pm returns are charged an additional day'. The $20.00/ski-day figure is arithmetically correct.
verification.also_confirmed: The tier ladder was claimed from a different page than the cited source_url, so it was checked separately on the shop's main site: Junior $35/day, Adult Basic $45/day, Adult Sport $70/day, Adult Performance $90/day ('Skis, Boots (90 Flex or higher), and Poles') - all confirmed, as is 'By Appointment Only' and 'Reservations may be made on this website as well as appointments for fitting of your equipment.' The claim that multi-day brackets are published for the Basic tier ONLY is also confirmed.
verification.caveat: The page carries no season-year label of any kind and no season date range beyond the 'Season Lease' product. The claim states this honestly. Treat $80 as the currently posted rate, not an explicitly 26/27-labelled one.

findings.name: Outback Adventures (Fremont) — best multi-day rate card in the Bay Area, but still showing LAST season
findings.claim: 44815 Industrial Drive, Fremont, CA 94538, 'Shop Open Seasonally', marketing itself to 'Fremont, San Jose, Hayward, the East Bay'. Its rate card is the most explicit and most trip-shaped in the region, with a genuine 4-5 Day column. Downhill Ski: Sport Ski Package (Recreational Skis, Recreational Boots, Poles) 1 Day $44 / 2 Day $58 / 3 Day $73 / 4-5 Day $94 / 6-7 Day $118 / 8-10 Day $147. Performance Ski Package 1/2/3/4-5 Day = $53 / $71 / $89 / $115. Junior Ski Package 4-5 Day $75. Snowboard Package (Snowboard, Boots, Strap Bindings) matches the Sport ski line exactly at 4-5 Day $94; Junior Snowboard 4-5 Day $75. Helmet 4-5 Day $21; Jacket/Pants/Bibs $26 each; ski/snowboard car racks 4-5 Day $39; roof box $78. A 4-ski-day trip is $94 sport / $115 performance = $23.50 and $28.75 per ski day. The shop explains its day-counting more clearly than anyone: 'We give FREE Pick-Up AND Return Days for all ski and snowboard equipment rentals. For example, if you are picking up gear on a Friday and returning it on a Monday, you will be charged a 2 day rental rate. The prices you see in the 2 day column are not a per day charge, it is for the entire time period... You can return your gear up until we close the store on your return day unlike other shops that require you to return by 1 or 2 pm or get additionally charged. We literally have the best ski and snowboard rental rates in the Bay Area.' THE CATCH, AND IT IS THE WHOLE POINT: the page is headed 'Ski and Snowboard Rental Package Rates 2025-2026 Season' and immediately below, 'Last ski/snowboard rental day pickup - April 4th, 2026'. As of 2026-08-27 this is LAST SEASON'S sheet still posted. Outback has not published 2026-27 rates. Do not carry these numbers forward as 26/27 pricing.
findings.price_usd: $94 for 4-5 days (Sport Ski or Snowboard Package); $115 Performance; $75 Junior — all 2025-26 season prices
findings.restrictions: PRICES ARE 2025-26, NOT 2026-27 — the shop has not posted next-season rates. Fremont is ~20 miles north of San Jose, a real detour but roughly on the way to I-680/I-80. 'Shop Open Seasonally', so it may not even be open when the group books. 'during holiday periods there is a 2 day rate minumum'. Late fee is steep and per-day: $25/day sport, $30/day performance. Reservations encouraged but not mandatory.
findings.season_confirmed: 2025-26 — stated explicitly on the page as 'Ski and Snowboard Rental Package Rates 2025-2026 Season' with last pickup April 4th, 2026. No 2026-27 pricing published as of 2026-08-27.
findings.drive_time_from_san_jose: ~20 mi / ~25 min from downtown San Jose via I-880 to Fremont. Roughly on the way to the I-680/I-80 corridor toward Donner Summit.

verification.why: Every number is transcribed correctly - Sport Ski $44/$58/$73/$94/$118/$147, Performance $53/$71/$89/$115 (and $144 / $180 at 6-7 and 8-10 day), Junior 4-5 day $75, Snowboard 4-5 day $94, Helmet 4-5 day $21 - but the page is still headed verbatim 'Ski and Snowboard Rental Package Rates 2025-2026 Season' with 'Last ski/snowboard rental day pickup - April 4th, 2026'. findings.name: California Ski Company (Berkeley) — cheapest 4-day rate found anywhere, but not South Bay
findings.claim: A Berkeley ski specialist with a clean four-tier rate card using the same bracket structure as Sports Basement. Adults Standard Package: 1 day $45, '2-4 days' $70, '5-9 days' $155, Seasonal (10/1 - 4/30) $350 — described as 'Budget friendly choice for novice to intermediate skiers who are comfortable on green terrain and easy groomed blue and black terrain.' Premium Package: $60 / $95 / $205 / $450. Elite Package (custom skis 'built by Wagner Custom Skis'): $100 / $200 / $350 / $600. Backcountry + Skins: $150 / $270 / $570. Juniors Standard: $35 / $55 / $120 / $250. At $70 for the 2-4 day bracket, a 4-ski-day Standard package is $17.50/day — the cheapest 4-day figure found in this entire research pass, about 18% under Sports Basement. Pickup policy is generous and stated verbatim: 'Your gear pickup day is always a "free" day—you can even pick up as early as 3:00 PM the day before your reservation.' The geography is the problem: Berkeley is ~50 miles from San Jose. For a San Jose group it is a genuine detour, though it does sit on the I-80 corridor toward Donner Summit, so a group already routing through the East Bay could collect gear en route. À la carte is also priced (Standard skis alone 2-4 days $60, Standard boots 2-4 days $40, helmet 2-4 days $25).
findings.price_usd: $70 for 2-4 days (Adults Standard Package); $45 1 day; $155 for 5-9 days; $350 seasonal
findings.restrictions: Berkeley, not South Bay — ~50 miles from San Jose. Only worth it for a group already heading up the I-80 corridor via the East Bay. Package tiers are ski-focused; the published package table shows no dedicated snowboard package, so a boarder in the group may not be servable here. Seasonal term is given as '10/1 - 4/30' with no year attached. No deposit requirement is mentioned anywhere on the page. RETURN DEADLINE (verified 2026-08-27): return days are free only 'as long as you're here before 1:00 p.m.'; returns after 1:00 p.m. are charged for that day, which would tip a 4-day rental into the 5-9 day bracket at $155. Berkeley by 1 p.m. on getaway day is a hard constraint for a group driving back from Tahoe. First-time fitting takes 30-60 minutes per person, once per season.
findings.season_confirmed: Not stated. Page carries no season-year label; the seasonal lease window is written as '10/1 - 4/30' with no year. Page was last published/crawled 2026-06-19 and rates were live 2026-08-27.
findings.drive_time_from_san_jose: ~50 mi / ~55 min from San Jose to Berkeley via I-880. A real detour, but it sits on the I-80 corridor toward Donner Summit, so an East Bay routing can collect gear en route.

verification.why: Adults Standard Package confirmed exactly on the live page: 1 day $45, Weekend 2-4 days $70, Week 5-9 days $155, Seasonal 10/1-4/30 $350. Premium ($60/$95/$205/$450), Elite ($100/$200/$350/$600), Backcountry+Skins ($150/$270/$570) and Juniors Standard ($35/$55/$120/$250) all check out, as do a la carte Standard skis 2-4 days $60 and Standard boots 2-4 days $40. $17.50/ski day is correct and this remains the cheapest verified 4-day rate found.
verification.material_omission_corrected: The finding quotes only the PICKUP half of the shop's free-day policy and therefore understates a real constraint. The live 'GEAR RETURN' section reads: 'Return days are also free, as long as you're here before 1:00 p.m. Returns after 1:00 p.m. are considered late and will be charged for that day; additional days past the return date will also incur a daily charge. Gear returned early will receive store credit for the unused days.' A 1:00 p.m. return deadline in BERKELEY is the tightest cutoff of any shop checked - tighter than Ski Renter's 2 p.m. and far tighter than Outback's return-by-closing. For a group driving back from Tahoe it means leaving the mountain early on the last day or paying an extra day, which would push a 4-day rental into the 5-9 day bracket at $155. That risk materially erodes the $70 headline advantage.
verification.also_noted: First-time renters should 'allow between 30 and 60 minutes for the fitting and gear selection process', once per season - a real cost for a party of six. No season-year label anywhere; the seasonal window is written '10/1 - 4/30' with no year.

findings.name: REI — still rents downhill packages nationally, but prices PER NIGHT with no free travel days
findings.claim: Contrary to the premise that several Bay Area chains have exited rental, REI's national rental pricing page still carries a full 'Downhill Snow Gear' table. Member pricing (no deposit required) vs non-member pricing ('$100-$200 per item deposit required at pick up'): Downhill Ski Packages - Adult Basic $34 first night / $18 additional night member, $51 / $27 non-member. Adult Premium $60 / $30 member. Youth $30 / $18. Snowboard Packages - Adult $34 / $18 member, Youth $24 / $14. Ski/Snowboard Helmets - Adult Basic $14 / $8. The structural difference that matters: REI charges by NIGHT, and there is no free-pickup-or-return-day concession anywhere on the page. A 5-night trip built around 4 ski days therefore costs a member $34 + 4x$18 = $106 ($26.50 per ski day) and a non-member $51 + 4x$27 = $159 ($39.75 per ski day) — meaningfully worse than Sports Basement's $85 flat, and the non-member number is nearly double. Even the most charitable 4-night reading is $34 + 3x$18 = $88. The page also warns: 'Please check with your local REI rental location on downhill snow gear availability and pricing.' That caveat is load-bearing here — the South Bay REI store pages for Saratoga (400 El Paseo de Saratoga, San Jose CA 95130) and Sunnyvale (130 E El Camino Real) describe an in-store 'Ski & Board Shop' offering tuning, waxing, binding mounts and repairs, and list no rental service at all. Downhill rental availability at a specific South Bay REI is therefore UNCONFIRMED and should be phoned before being relied on.
findings.price_usd: $106 for 5 nights / $88 for 4 nights (member, Adult Basic ski or snowboard package); $159 for 5 nights non-member
findings.per_day_usd: $26.50 member across 4 ski days on a 5-night trip; $39.75 non-member
findings.restrictions: Per-NIGHT pricing with no free transport days — the worst structure of any option here for a drive-up trip, because both travel nights are billable. Non-members pay ~50% more AND a '$100-$200 per item deposit required at pick up'; members pay no deposit. Availability is explicitly not guaranteed by store: 'Please check with your local REI rental location on downhill snow gear availability and pricing.' Neither the REI Saratoga nor REI Sunnyvale store page advertises rentals — both describe tuning/repair services only. Group note: 'Planning a trip for 10 or more people? Please call your local REI to confirm availability for large group rentals' — a 6-person group is under that threshold.
findings.season_confirmed: Not stated. REI's rental pricing page is a rolling national rate card with no season-year label. Live as of 2026-08-27.
findings.drive_time_from_san_jose: REI Saratoga is ~6 mi / ~12 min and REI Sunnyvale ~11 mi / ~18 min from San Jose - but neither store page advertises rentals, so the nearest confirmed rental counter is unknown.

verification.method: The Downhill Snow Gear table sits inside a collapsed accordion that WebFetch cannot open (plain fetch also returned ECONNRESET twice). Verified by expanding the accordion in a real browser and reading the rendered table.
verification.why: Every claimed figure matches the live table. Downhill Ski Packages - Adult Basic $34 first night / $18 additional (member) and $51 / $27 (non-member); Adult Premium $60 / $30 member; Youth $30 / $18; Snowboard Packages - Adult $34 / $18 member, Youth $24 / $14; Ski/Snowboard Helmets - Adult Basic $14 / $8. The member column is headed 'No deposit required' and the non-member column '$100-$200 per item deposit required at pick up', exactly as claimed. The page closes with the verbatim line 'Please check with your local REI rental location on downhill snow gear availability and pricing.' Derived totals are arithmetically right: 5 nights member $34 + 4x$18 = $106; non-member $51 + 4x$27 = $159; 4 nights $34 + 3x$18 = $88.

The structural point (per-night billing with no free transport days, making REI the worst fit for a drive-up trip) is confirmed by the table's shape.

findings.name: Mountain View Sports — South Bay, real online discount, but NO multi-day break at all
findings.claim: A Mountain View shop running a rentals portal with a walk-in vs online two-price structure — the online rate is a flat 20% off walk-in. Ski: Demo Package $64 walk-in / $51.20 online ('includes skis from Blizzard, Nordica, Atomic, Volkl, K2 and Rossignol'); Premium Package $50 / $40 ('newest gear with a wide selection of brands and sizes'); Sport Package $39 / $31.20 ('equipment has been used for a few seasons but is well maintained'); Junior Ski Package (12 and under) $26 / $20.80 ('Skis, boots and poles'); Junior Performance $32 / $25.60. Snowboard: Demo Snowboard Package $64 / $51.20 ('Never Summer' boards); Adult Snowboard Package $50 / $40 ('Arbor, K2, Elan and Salomon' with 'Salomon binding systems'); Junior Snowboard $32 / $25.60. Adult ski or snowboard boot only $26 / $20.80. THE PROBLEM: every price is quoted per day and the site publishes no multi-day bracket or discount whatsoever. A 4-ski-day Sport package therefore costs 4 x $31.20 = $124.80 online, or $156 walk-in — versus $85 at Sports Basement for comparable-or-better basic gear. Unless a multi-day rate exists that is simply unpublished, this is the worst value in the South Bay for a 4-day trip and roughly 47% more than Sports Basement. Worth a phone call only if the group specifically wants Never Summer demo boards.
findings.price_usd: $124.80 online / $156.00 walk-in for 4 days (Sport ski package), derived by multiplying the published daily rate — NO multi-day rate is published
findings.per_day_usd: $31.20 online / $39.00 walk-in (Sport); $40.00 online (Premium ski or Adult Snowboard); $51.20 online (Demo)
findings.restrictions: No multi-day discount published anywhere — the 4-day total above is a multiplication of the daily rate, not a quoted package price, so treat the total as derived rather than posted. Online booking is required to get the 20% discount. 'Ski and Snowboard Pants' are 'Not available for reservation'. Snowshoes are 'first come first serve basis'. No deposit, no season dates and no store address are stated on the rentals portal.
findings.season_confirmed: Not stated. The rentals portal carries no season-year label and no season date range. Live as of 2026-08-27.
findings.drive_time_from_san_jose: ~13 mi / ~20 min from downtown San Jose. In-town pickup.

verification.why: Every published daily rate matches: Ski Demo $64 walk-in / $51.20 online, Premium $50 / $40, Sport $39 / $31.20, Junior Ski $26 / $20.80, Junior Performance $32 / $25.60, Demo Snowboard $64 / $51.20, Adult Snowboard $50 / $40, Junior Snowboard $32 / $25.60, adult ski or snowboard boot only $26 / $20.80. The 20%-off-online structure holds across every line. Critically, the claim that NO multi-day rate, weekly rate or multi-day discount is published anywhere on the portal is confirmed - all pricing is daily.
verification.caveat: The $124.80 / $156.00 four-day totals are NOT posted anywhere; they are the daily rate multiplied by four. The finding already discloses this in both the price field and the restrictions, which is the correct handling, and confidence is already 'medium'. Left as-is. If this number reaches the site it must keep the 'derived, not quoted' caption, since a shop with no published multi-day rate may well quote one by phone.

findings.name: Structural finding: rent in the South Bay, not at the resort — but check the resort number first
findings.claim: Every South Bay shop researched here sells the same pitch, and Sports Basement states it plainly on its rates page: 'Say no way to long lines at the resort rentals counter! Save time and money when you rent skis and snowboards at Sports Basement before you head to Tahoe.' The pricing structure backs the claim up for a multi-day trip specifically, and the mechanism is the free-transport-day convention plus flat duration brackets. Three of the four cheap shops state the convention in their own words — Sports Basement ('your pickup and return days are free'), Outback Adventures ('We give FREE Pick-Up AND Return Days'), California Ski Company ('Your gear pickup day is always a "free" day—you can even pick up as early as 3:00 PM the day before your reservation'), and Ski Renter of Mountain View ('We do not count the Pickup day or Return day by 2pm as rental days'). REI is the conspicuous exception, charging per night with both travel nights billable, which is why its effective rate is 25-85% worse than Sports Basement despite a competitive-looking $34 headline. IMPORTANT CAVEAT FOR THE SITE: this dimension establishes what the South Bay costs, NOT that South Bay beats the resort. The repo's recent history shows a decision to 'Recommend renting gear at the resort', and this research does not overturn it on its own — the comparison needs the resort-side 4-day rental number, which is outside this dimension's scope. What this research does establish is the correct South Bay benchmark to compare against: $85 flat for 4 days basic, $110 sport, from a store in Sunnyvale or Campbell. If a resort's 4-day package beats $85, rent at the resort; if it does not, the pre-trip pickup wins and also removes a morning queue.
findings.price_usd: $85 (Sports Basement Adult Basic, 2-4 days) is the South Bay benchmark any resort rental price should be compared against
findings.restrictions: This finding deliberately does NOT claim South Bay beats resort rental — no resort rental price was fetched in this dimension. It supplies only the South Bay side of that comparison. Also note the logistics cost the price table hides: six people need six boot fittings before departure, which is a real hour or two and, at Ski Renter of Mountain View, requires an appointment. Renting at the resort trades money for that time; renting in town trades time for money. RETURN CUTOFFS ARE NOT UNIFORM (verified 2026-08-27): Outback allows return until store close; Ski Renter requires 2 p.m.; California Ski Company requires before 1:00 p.m. or the day is charged; Sports Basement publishes no return clock. On a drive-home day this determines whether the trip bills inside the cheap bracket.
findings.season_confirmed: Live posted rates as of 2026-08-27; season-year labeling varies by shop as noted in each finding.
findings.drive_time_from_san_jose: South Bay pickup shops cluster 7-14 mi from downtown San Jose; the Tahoe drive itself is ~200-210 mi / ~3h35m via I-80.

verification.why: The $85 benchmark is confirmed against the live Sports Basement table, and the framing quote is verbatim on the rates page: 'SAY NO WAY TO LONG LINES AT THE RESORT RENTALS COUNTER! SAVE TIME AND MONEY WHEN YOU RENT SKIS AND SNOWBOARDS AT SPORTS BASEMENT BEFORE YOU HEAD TO TAHOE.' All four free-transport-day quotes are accurate as quoted, and the REI exception is confirmed by REI's own per-night table. The finding's discipline in NOT claiming South Bay beats the resort is correct and should be preserved.
verification.correction: The finding presents the free-transport-day convention as roughly uniform across the four cheap shops. It is not - the RETURN cutoffs differ sharply, and that difference decides whether a 4-ski-day trip actually bills as a 4-day rental. Sports Basement states pickup and return days free with no published clock; Outback Adventures is most generous, 'You can return your gear up until we close the store on your return day'; Ski Renter of Mountain View requires return by 2 p.m. or charges an extra day; California Ski Company requires return before 1:00 p.m. ('Return days are also free, as long as you're here before 1:00 p.m.'), the tightest of the four. For a group driving home from Tahoe on the last day, a 1 p.m. Berkeley deadline is the difference between the $70 weekend bracket and the $155 week bracket. The convention is real but not uniform, and the caption should say so.
verification.also_noted: The free-days quote attributed to Sports Basement lives on a page titled 'Snow Season Prep Guide: 2025/26 Edition', still the live guide on the site as of 2026-08-27. The policy is a standing convention rather than a 26/27 restatement.
